title: Public-support identifiability audit for executable graph routing
question: Is the target executable program identifiable from the router-visible support examples under the registered graph-candidate generator, before learned routing is evaluated?
hypothesis: Four public truth-table support rows are insufficient to uniquely identify the target in a nontrivial fraction of candidate pools; increasing the registered support set should reduce support-equivalent candidate multiplicity. This is a benchmark identifiability audit, not evidence about learned routing quality.

arms.name: support_identifiability
arms.intervention: measure target-consistent candidate multiplicity for prespecified public support sizes

arms.name: behavior_index_control
arms.intervention: retrieve support-consistent candidates using an exact inverted index over candidate truth-table behavior computed from public executable graphs

endpoints.name: expected_uniform_tie_success
endpoints.role: diagnostic upper-bound reference under uniform choice among support-equivalent candidates

decision_rule.condition: At support_size=4, target_unique_fraction is low or support_consistent_count materially exceeds 1.
decision_rule.licenses: a benchmark identifiability warning: the target is not generally determined by the router-visible evidence under the registered candidate generator.
decision_rule.does_not_license: a negative conclusion about learned routing, graph representations, CASM, or PLM.

decision_rule.condition: Support_size sweep shows target_unique_fraction increasing toward 1 while the candidate universe and target generation remain fixed.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that public support information, rather than optimizer changes, controls target identifiability on this synthetic benchmark.

decision_rule.condition: The exact behavior index reproduces the scan-derived support-consistent set at every tested cell.
decision_rule.licenses: a deterministic semantic-addressing control for candidate behavior under the registered executable-graph workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: sublinear hardware speedup or learned semantic routing.

held_constant: the pinned CASM BooleanDAGGenerator commit c31554413301e3c9d3e6b3f8c8c6be572a74a748
the graph-candidate generator and exact executable graph semantics from G-CASM-010
train_programs=256 with exact structure and truth-signature exclusion
the candidate pool is generated once per task and reused across all support sizes
support rows are selected from one deterministic permutation per task and prefixes of size 4,8,12,16 are evaluated
the target index, target structure ID, verifier-only rows, and hidden truth table are not used by the query operation
no learned router is trained or tuned in this experiment

behavior_index.construction: execute every candidate graph over all 16 input assignments and insert each (input_assignment, output_bit) pair into an inverted posting list
behavior_index.query: intersect the posting lists for the observed support rows
behavior_index.target_information: none beyond the public support rows and public candidate graphs
behavior_index.build_work: sum exact graph execution operations for all candidates and all 16 input assignments
behavior_index.query_work: posting entries inspected plus set-intersection operations
behavior_index.semantic_control: index result must exactly equal a linear scan for every support size

promotion_rule: all candidate truth signatures are unique within each generated pool
linear-scan support-consistency and inverted-index support-consistency agree for every task/support size
candidate pool is unchanged across support-size comparisons
no target index or verifier-only row enters the query function
raw task-level counts are retained in the artifact
no learned capability or asymptotic-complexity claim is made
